title:
When the pumps stop,
the plan matters.
caption: MajiShift helps an operator compare pumping plans before an interruption puts essential water reserves under pressure.

title: Built by Brian & Patrick
caption: Brian Mwangi: backend engineering, Adaption model training and data aggregation. Patrick Leon: frontend development, UI/UX, QA and GIS.

title: One reservoir. Competing needs.
caption: Essential use, irrigation and pumping availability all draw on the same limited water balance. Operators need to see the trade-offs.

title: A decision before an interruption
caption: Our JKUAT pilot exploration asks a practical question: can a proposed schedule maintain a minimum reserve through two unavailable pumping days?

title: Real observations. Explicit assumptions.
caption: The historical replay uses official Conduit station 61 observations from 29 August to 4 September 2026. Operating values remain synthetic.

title: Temperature becomes a planning input
caption: Daily temperature ranges drive a Hargreaves reference evapotranspiration estimate. Measured rain also enters the water balance; this replay recorded no rain.

title: 35.6 m³ changes the storage balance
caption: Compared with four millimetres per day, Conduit weather adds 35.6 cubic metres of estimated loss. Total default pumping remains unchanged.

title: Start with the operating assumptions
caption: This example starts with 9,000 cubic metres in storage, a 5,000 cubic metre reserve, and essential demand of 1,400 cubic metres daily.

title: Prepare for two unavailable days
caption: Pumping is unavailable on days two and three. The fixed schedule pumps four hours on available days; the proposed plan prepares a buffer.

title: Two plans. One water balance.
caption: Both schedules use the same weather and operating assumptions. The teal line follows the proposed schedule; the dashed line follows the fixed schedule.

title: The reserve is the decision threshold
caption: In this scenario, the fixed schedule falls below the reserve on five days. The proposed schedule stays above the reserve throughout.

title: Inspect the trade-off
caption: The proposed plan pumps 7,875 cubic metres versus 5,000 for the fixed schedule. This protects the reserve through more pumping, not water savings.

title: A recommendation you can inspect
caption: Day one calls for 4.5 hours of pumping. Days two and three correctly show zero pumping because equipment is unavailable.

title: Essential demand comes first
caption: The table exposes each day’s rain, estimated loss, pumping hours and ending storage. Unserved irrigation and unmet essential demand are tracked explicitly.

title: What if starting storage is lower?
caption: Now reduce starting storage from 9,000 to 8,000 cubic metres and compare again. The same weather and outage assumptions remain in place.

title: The recommendation responds
caption: Day-one pumping rises from 4.5 to 8.5 hours. The revised plan builds the same outage buffer from a lower starting level.

title: Export the complete scenario
caption: Export saves the inputs, weather provenance and calculated schedules as JSON. That gives the operator a record to review and share.

title: A transparent calculation
caption: React and TypeScript present the planner and GIS view. A shared water-balance module compares schedules; the historical weather replay supplies daily inputs.

title: Separate the prototype from the research
caption: Adaption model-training experiments are a separate research track. The working schedules shown here come from the transparent planner, not a served AI model.

title: Make trade-offs visible before acting
caption: The intended benefit is earlier preparation and clearer reserve planning. These scenario results are not measured campus savings or evidence of field performance.

title: Validate with the operator
caption: Next: approved operating records, calibrated surface-loss estimates and pilot evaluation. Reference evapotranspiration is a proxy, not measured reservoir evaporation.

title:
Keep the reserve.
Plan the next move.
caption: MajiShift. From environmental observations to an inspectable water-planning decision.
